learner: CS graduate; familiar with Linux, programming and Git; new to cloud and DevOps; 14 hours per week
inspection_scope: All ten repository README files and GitHub file inventories; selected teaching, test and deployment files as recorded per repository. No repository code executed and no cloud resources created. Inventory completeness does not imply all files were read.

repositories.observed_structure: Markdown guides plus JSON exercises, quizzes, flashcards and checklists; app source, Docker configuration and tests.
repositories.use: Read one relevant exercise, reproduce the concept in the continuing project, then extend it with a failure and acceptance checks.
repositories.deliverable: Measured image improvement; reviewed VPC plan; idempotent server configuration; deployment and cleanup evidence.
adaptations: VPC example provisions NAT gateways per availability zone and repeatedly uses apply -auto-approve. Estimate cost and review saved plans before applying.
Ansible example disables host-key checking and uses a latest version variable. Enroll trusted SSH host keys and use a tested update/version policy.
Tutorial duration estimates are not competency gates. Verify current versions and provider behavior.
repositories.stop_rule: One exercise per current capability; do not browse unrelated daily content during lab time.

repositories.observed_structure: 140 DevOps Markdown content files; live serialized graph 171 nodes including 139 topics/subtopics and 60 explicit display edges; live DOM 173 groups due to two additional legend items.
repositories.use: Review selected branches against evidence from completed labs, keeping alternative tools as optional awareness topics.
repositories.deliverable: Topic coverage with can-explain, built, broke-and-repaired and operated-with-evidence states.
adaptations: Live legend explicitly indicates alternatives and nonstrict order; this is not a prerequisite-ordered course.
GitLab node provides introduction and links; GitLab runner security, identity federation, rollback and test gates need dedicated labs.
Add explicit unit/integration/system testing, recovery, costs, incident work and data migration threads.
Do not infer website deployment identity from repository HEAD; retained source and live evidence are separate.
repositories.stop_rule: Keep the handbook's sequence; do not complete every technology shown.

repositories.observed_structure: Topic directories with questions, practical exercises and some solutions; substantial AWS/Terraform content and smaller GCP sections.
repositories.use: Answer 5–10 questions after a matching lab without opening solutions. Reproduce every failed answer as an experiment.
repositories.deliverable: Answer, prediction, experiment output and corrected explanation for each misconception.
adaptations: Some AWS exercises cost money, and the source explicitly notes this.
Console answers can be translated into Terraform after learning the underlying service.
CI examples include Jenkins; preserve learning objectives while implementing GitLab.
Question count and recalled answers do not measure operating competence.
repositories.stop_rule: Select only current and review topics; stop after resolving misconceptions rather than completing the entire bank.

repositories.observed_structure: Thirteen labs spanning machines, certificates, kubeconfig, encryption, etcd, controllers, workers, routing, smoke testing and cleanup.
repositories.use: After Kubernetes operational basics, bootstrap the training cluster and explain every identity, component and request boundary.
repositories.deliverable: Architecture and trust diagram, encryption/probe/service smoke-test evidence, one diagnosed fault and cleanup record.
adaptations: Observed README uses Kubernetes v1.32.x, containerd v2.1.x, CNI v1.6.x and etcd v3.6.x. These are observed tutorial versions, not current production recommendations.
Four Debian 12 ARM64/AMD64 machines are required; one control-plane server means this is not a highly available architecture.
The README explicitly states its result is not production ready.
Allow two weeks or extend the schedule if the learner cannot explain each step; do not rush by pasting commands.
repositories.stop_rule: Finish the bounded internals study and cleanup; use managed or supported operational designs for the main cloud project.

repositories.observed_structure: 2022 foundations, 2023 DevSecOps and 2024 community content, with translations and supporting assets.
repositories.use: Choose 2022 days 42–47 for containers, 56–62 for IaC, 63–69 for Ansible and selected monitoring/recovery chapters; use 2023 security, secrets, databases and operations sections.
repositories.deliverable: One applied change or tested hypothesis per selected chapter, recorded in the continuing project.
adaptations: 2022 cloud lessons focus on Azure; CI lessons focus on Jenkins/GitHub Actions. Substitute AWS/GCP and GitLab deliberately.
The chapter indexes were inspected; individual day lessons were not all read or executed.
Validate dated commands and versions against current project documentation.
90 days is the source author's structure, not this learner's deadline.
repositories.stop_rule: Do not add all chapters on top of the 52-week schedule; choose chapters that serve the current lab.

repositories.observed_structure: Main resource README, roadmap image and PDF; twelve subject sections and DevSecOps additions.
repositories.use: Compare completed capability evidence with its major categories during quarterly review.
repositories.deliverable: A prioritized missing-capability list and one justification for a tool choice.
adaptations: Its resource list is not a tested lab sequence.
It includes paid and free learning resources; purchasing anything is optional.
Keep software engineering practices and security in the main path rather than postponing them.
repositories.stop_rule: 30-minute scope review; do not start a second parallel curriculum.

repositories.observed_structure: Dedicated directories for learning resources, official resources, installers, projects and managed Kubernetes.
repositories.use: Start with one question, shortlist at most two options, and validate against their official documentation.
repositories.deliverable: A short architecture decision describing requirements, costs, maintenance and the rejected option.
adaptations: Historical articles and platform names remain in the list.
Directory inclusion does not establish maintenance, compatibility or security.
Do not add service mesh, multiple ingress products and extra operators without a concrete need.
repositories.stop_rule: Use the directory to answer a current design question; avoid broad tool collection.

repositories.role: Reliability, incident work and operational judgment
repositories.observed_structure: Curated reading organized by culture, reliability, observability, on-call, postmortems, capacity, service levels and performance.
repositories.use: Select one primary SRE chapter or operator case study, then apply it through an incident or measurement exercise.
repositories.deliverable: SLO specification, actionable alert, runbook, incident timeline, postmortem and verified follow-up improvement.
adaptations: Reading is paired with the learner's own evidence.
Some links are historical; use current primary destinations where available.
Simulated on-call experience must be described as simulation.
repositories.stop_rule: At most one assigned reading per operational exercise; depth comes from measured behavior and reflection.

repositories.role: Platform reference workload and test specimen
repositories.observed_structure: Go HTTP/gRPC APIs and tests, Helm/Kustomize deployment assets, CI workflows and cluster integration tests.
repositories.use: Use it to isolate platform problems, then transfer its tested practices to the learner's business application.
repositories.deliverable: GitLab translation of relevant test stages; readiness and rollout experiments; a fault-injection incident with metrics and recovery evidence.
adaptations: The app intentionally exposes /env, /configs, /panic and fault controls; keep it private with dummy values.
Workflow labels use both integration and end-to-end terms; classify your tests by the actual boundary they exercise.
Its ready-made application does not replace business-rule, database migration or recovery testing of the main project.
Inspect the tested source revision rather than copying an unpinned latest chart.
repositories.stop_rule: Use the reference workload until the platform behavior is understood; repeat the important checks on the continuing project.

repositories.observed_structure: Broad categorized directory including registries, CI/CD, observability, secrets, security, chaos and developer platforms.
repositories.use: Use a category to find two candidates for a real requirement and continue in primary project documentation.
repositories.deliverable: A decision record with the operational cost of adopting the chosen tool.
adaptations: Tags and list membership do not verify license suitability, maintenance or secure defaults.
Limit fault experiments to the owned lab and document scope and stop conditions.
The selected stack remains stable unless evidence warrants a change.
repositories.stop_rule: 30 minutes to shortlist; stop browsing and test a decision.
